summary: Mobile emulation (393x852) on /thesis + /thesis/co_plan_ui: NO horizontal document scroll in any mode (company, explore, treemap, all explore-view tabs, radar toggled). document.scrollWidth == window.innerWidth == 393 in every scan. Detail /thesis/co_plan_ui: 0 overflowing descendants. Desktop (1280x800) regression: sticky sidebar is BROKEN — the aside[data-testid=thesis-sidebar] still has position:sticky computed, but after scrollTo(0,600) its bounding top went from 143 to -456 (should have stuck near top:16). Root cause is almost certainly the overflowX:'clip' inline style added to the [data-testid=thesis-page] root: overflow:clip on an ancestor establishes a containment context that prevents descendant position:sticky from anchoring to the viewport (same behavior as overflow:hidden on an ancestor).

ui_bugs.issue: aside[data-testid=thesis-sidebar] with lg:sticky lg:top-4 no longer sticks on desktop. Before scroll top=143, after window.scrollTo(0,600) top=-456 (scrolls away with page). Computed position is 'sticky' but has no effect. Regression caused by overflowX:'clip' inline style on the [data-testid=thesis-page] root wrapper (Thesis.jsx line 545). overflow-x:clip on an ancestor creates a scroll containment context that disables descendant position:sticky vs. the viewport (browsers treat clip/hidden ancestors as the nearest scroll container).

overflowing_descendants.note: Intentional horizontal scroller wrapping the explore-view tabs (Megatendencias/Tendencias/Convergencia). Its own overflow-x-auto is by design; does not affect document scroll.
The tabs bar inside the above scroller — this is what makes the scroller needed (contained, expected).
Last tab, sits inside the horizontal scroller — expected.

diagnostic_scan_results.mobile_thesis_explore_mode: Same 3 elements as company mode; docSW=393. Treemap w-full overflow-hidden works correctly.

mobile_explore_tab_convergence.note: Only 1 element flagged (the parent overflow-x-auto scroller). No real overflow.

extra_overflowing.note: Toast/sonner container extends ~16px past viewport; does not propagate to document scrollWidth (likely fixed-positioned).

root_cause_confirmation: The user-reported horizontal overflow on /thesis is now effectively eliminated at the document level thanks to overflowX:'clip' on thesis-page. The remaining descendants that report scrollWidth>clientWidth on mobile are all inside a deliberate overflow-x-auto wrapper around the explore-view tabs (MEGATENDENCIAS/TENDENCIAS/CONVERGENCIA), which is intended UX (allows swiping the tab strip). The underlying element that was making the whole page overflow before was almost certainly this same tabs bar (div.flex.border.border-black.w-fit, natural width ~452px) which used to bubble up before the scroller wrapper / min-w-0 / clip fixes were added. HOWEVER: the clip on the root has broken desktop sticky on the sidebar.
recommended_fixes_for_main_agent: Replace overflowX:'clip' on [data-testid=thesis-page] with a scope that doesn't break sticky. Options: (a) apply overflow-x:clip only on <body> or only on a wrapper that is NOT an ancestor of the sticky element — e.g. wrap only the <main> column, not the whole grid; (b) leave root as overflow-x:visible and rely on the min-w-0 fixes + the explicit overflow-x-auto around the tabs bar (which is already the true culprit); (c) use overflow-clip-margin or set overflow-x:clip only at mobile breakpoint with a media query so lg:+ keeps overflow visible and sticky works.

Preferred: make root overflow visible and instead ensure the explore-tabs wrapper (div.min-w-0.max-w-full.overflow-x-auto) is the only horizontal scroller. Because docSW==393 came from that wrapper working, the clip may no longer be necessary.
action_items: Fix desktop sticky regression on ThesisSidebar caused by overflowX:'clip' on thesis-page root. See recommended_fixes_for_main_agent.
Optional: also apply overflow-x-clip / min-w-0 on the OL toast container root so it doesn't visually extend past the viewport when Radar toggle shows a toast (cosmetic, does not cause page scroll).
critical_code_review_comments: Thesis.jsx: overflowX:'clip' on the root grid container is a viable last-resort clamp but disables position:sticky in descendants. Prefer scoping horizontal clipping to a container that is NOT an ancestor of the sticky aside.

There are two aside[data-testid=thesis-sidebar] elements (Thesis.jsx L828 for logged-out, ThesisSidebar.jsx L204 for logged-in). Only the logged-in one has lg:sticky lg:top-4 — acceptable, but the logged-out one loses sticky behavior silently.
The explore-view tab strip uses w-fit inside overflow-x-auto — good pattern; keep this and remove root-level clip.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mobile overflow issue on /thesis is resolved at document level. Focus next iteration on verifying desktop sticky sidebar behavior after main agent removes/scopes the overflowX:'clip'. Use cookie session_token=test_profile_token_fixed_123, viewport 1280x800, scroll to y=600 and confirm [data-testid=thesis-sidebar] getBoundingClientRect().top stays near 16 (top-4).
rca_of_the_issue: Mobile horizontal scroll RCA: the explore-view tab strip (div.flex.border.border-black.w-fit containing MEGATENDENCIAS/TENDENCIAS/CONVERGENCIA buttons) has a natural width ~452px which exceeded the 393px viewport and was propagating to the document. Fix chain applied by main agent (min-w-0 on grid children + overflow-x-auto wrapper around the tabs + overflowX:'clip' on root) all contribute; the tabs wrapper is the key structural fix. Reproduction on real device would require Explore mode being visible. Detail page /thesis/co_plan_ui had no overflow. Desktop sticky regression RCA: overflow:clip on the [data-testid=thesis-page] ancestor establishes containment that disables descendant position:sticky.
